To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Cancer survivors are at risk for osteopenia/osteoporosis; (2) Bisphosphonate use decreases bone loss in cancer patients at risk; (3) Bisphosphnates decrease fracture risk in breast cancer patients; (4) Aromatase inhibitors increase bone loss in breast cancer patients.
patients treated with aromatase inhibitors for breast cancer or with chemotherapy for prostate cancer are at increased risk for osteoporotic fracture.
cancer treatment-induced bone losses are common and can lead to fractures and that treatment with calcium, Vitamin D and bisphosphnates can prevent bone loss.

the development of new, efficient, and environmentally friendly methods for the synthesis of biologically active compounds.
the development and characterization of a new class of materials for the treatment of bone cancer.
the development and application of new and improved methods of cancer diagnosis and therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the treatment of cancer treatment-induced osteoporosis and osteopenia should be a standard of care.
the treatment of osteoporosis in cancer patients is a very complex and challenging area that is in need of further study.
cancer patients at risk for osteopenia or osteoporosis should receive calcium, vitamin D and bisphosphonorates to prevent fracture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the risk of osteoporotic fracture is high in cancer patients.
cancer survivors are at risk of osteoporosis, and treatment with calcium, vit D and/or bisphosphonate will decrease their risk.
the risk of osteoporosis and fractures is increased in patients who have received cancer treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients treated for cancer should be evaluated for bone loss and treated if necessary.
we should be screening for bone loss and osteoporosis in cancer survivors and treating those who have bone loss.
patients at risk for cancer treatment-induced bone losses should be treated to prevent fractures.
